questions.text:
Consider the following transaction involving two bank accounts x and y.

read(x); x:=x-50; write(x); read(y); y:=y+50; write(y)

The constraint that the sum of the accounts x and y should remain constant is that of
questions.solution:
Keeping x + y constant is an integrity rule of the database, which the transaction must preserve. That is the consistency property.

Answer: Consistency

questions.text:
With reference to the B+ tree index of order 1 shown below, the minimum number of nodes (including the Root node) that must be fetched in order to satisfy the following query:
"Get all records with a search key greater than or equal to 7 and less than 15"
is ____________.
questions.solution:
Search for 7: root (9) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] left internal node (5) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] leaf [5, 7].

Then follow leaf links: [9, 11] and [13, 15], where 15 shows we can stop.

Nodes = root + 1 internal + 3 leaves = 5

Answer: 5

questions.text: Identify the correct order in which a server process must invoke the function calls accept, bind, listen, and recv according to UNIx socket API.
questions.solution:
Server side: socket, then bind (attach address), listen (become passive), accept (take a connection), recv (read data).

Answer: bind, listen, accept, recv

questions.text: A link has a transmission speed of [latex]10^{6}[/latex] bits/sec. It uses data packets of size 1000 bytes each. Assume that the acknowledgment has negligible transmission delay, and that its propagation delay is the same as the data propagation delay. Also assume that the processing delays at nodes are negligible. The efficiency of the stop-and-wait protocol in this setup is exactly 25%. The value of the one-way propagation delay (in milliseconds) is ________.
questions.solution:
[latex]T_t=\frac{8000}{10^6}=8[/latex] ms.

[latex]\eta=\frac{T_t}{T_t+2T_p}=0.25\Rightarrow 8+2T_p=32\Rightarrow T_p=12[/latex] ms

Answer: 12

questions.text: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct about HTTP cookies?
questions.solution:
A cookie is a small piece of data (name-value text) stored by the browser, not executable code.

It does come in the Set-Cookie HTTP header, has an expiry time and can track browsing on a site.

Answer: A cookie is a piece of code that has the potential to compromise security
